title: Code, results and pre-registration for: Equation discovery fails before rate constants become unidentifiable in simulated adsorption columns
description: A pre-registered computational study of when equation-discovery methods recover the kinetic law of an adsorption column from its outlet and profile data. Ground truth comes from a verified finite-difference solver (imported from the Paper 1 archive, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23323685). Sparse regression in weak and strong forms, exact best-subset selection, ensembles, errors-in-variables regression, symbolic regression and a neural network in the column model are compared, over a grid of Damkoehler number, Peclet number, noise, isotherm error and three observation models, against profile-likelihood identifiability of the rate constant. The pre-registration (PREREG_P2_discoverability.md) was frozen before any method ran on the grid; amendments A1 to A4 preceded the grid, A5 was made while it ran, and A6 and A7 (implementation corrections, RETRACTIONS_P2 B87, B89, B90) after the first verdicts, with every earlier result file kept. Exploratory analyses E1 to E11 (EXPLORATORY_P2.md, including E11 at about 2,000 observation times per run), declared before they ran (one undeclared diagnostic and one deviation are disclosed there), are reported separately from the confirmatory results. The commit history is kept here. Source Data for Figures 2 to 5 are in paper2/source_data/; results/freeze_push_evidence.json keeps GitHub's server-side record that the frozen pre-registration was public before the grid ran.
